title: Smallest Rectangle Enclosing Black Pixels
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix representing an image with 0s as white pixels and 1s as black pixels, where black pixels form a single connected region, and given coordinates (x, y) of a black pixel, find the area of the smallest rectangle aligned with the axes that encloses all black pixels.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix representing an image with 0s as white pixels and 1s as black pixels, where black pixels form a single connected region, and given coordinates (x, y) of a black pixel, find the area of the smallest rectangle aligned with the axes that encloses all black pixels. The algorithm must have a runtime complexity less than O(mn).
constraints: image is a rectangular 1–100 by 1–100 matrix of strings '0' and '1'. All black pixels form one four-direction connected region, and image[x][y] is '1'.
Return the area of the smallest axis-aligned rectangle containing every black pixel. The target running time must be better than scanning all mn cells.
target_time_complexity: O(m log n + n log m)
hints: Connectivity guarantees that the set of rows containing black is one interval, and the same is true for columns.
Use the known black row x and column y to split four monotone searches: first/last black row and first/last black column.
Binary-search whether a candidate row contains any black pixel; repeat for columns, then multiply the boundary differences.
Each row probe scans n cells and each column probe scans m, giving O(m log n+n log m), which is below O(mn) for the intended dimensions.
editorial: A four-direction connected black region cannot skip an entire row or column between two occupied ones, so occupied rows and columns each form contiguous intervals. The known black pixel lies inside both intervals. Binary searches find their lower and exclusive upper boundaries using row/column existence probes. Their spans determine the rectangle. The independent oracle scans every generated cell and directly takes minimum and maximum coordinates.

tests.explanation: Black rows span 0..2 and columns span 1..2, so the enclosing rectangle has area 3×2=6.
The connected L shape reaches both rows and both columns; its enclosing rectangle has area 4 even though only three pixels are black.
